set.display.drawing.help: How the scan is drawn. Auto: your device's preset (the line under this row says which one was picked), normally the classic sorted drawing, which is smooth and keeps the scan's detail; the site's owner can change the presets. Stochastic skips sorting the splats and leaves a fine grain: it is a single noisy sample per pixel, so it can look rough in rooms. Sorted is the classic, smooth drawing. A link with ?stochastic (or ?stochastic=0) is obeyed when a scene opens; a choice made here while flying wins for that scene. Stochastic needs WebGPU in a desktop browser. Recording and the video export always draw sorted.
set.display.budget.help: How many million splats the scan may draw at most. Auto takes the link's ?budget=, the scene owner's choice, or this device's preset (see the Render row). A link's ?budget= is obeyed when a scene opens; a choice made here while flying wins for that scene. More splats are sharper and slower; the quality governor still lowers it when frames are missed. Set it to what your device can do: it counts on a phone and a tablet too, up as well as down (a link's or a scene's number does not).
set.display.deviceClass.help: Which kind of device the site's drawing presets treat this as. Auto recognises it from the browser (the graphics adapter, memory, processor cores, touch screen and screen size); name the class yourself when the guess is wrong, for example a laptop that should draw like a strong desktop. The class sets the preset that Auto in Render and Splat budget stands for: the drawing, the splat budget and the resolution. You can still set Render and Splat budget by hand.
